A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Face Anything work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across appendix additions and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction, tracking, efficiency and ablation results in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds original loss-ablation, avatar-comparison, reconstruction-tuning and qualitative results.

M1.justification: The architecture, depth/ray/canonical predictions, training stages, final losses and nearest-neighbor tracking procedure are unchanged. The neighborhood-consistency loss is tested as an ablation, not adopted into the proposed method.

E1.justification: Appendix D adds qualitative evaluation using CelebV-Text and Hallo3 examples, including extreme lighting and out-of-distribution identities, plus explicit hair-motion and heavy-occlusion cases. The training datasets, original benchmarks and reconstruction/tracking tasks remain.

E2.justification: New Table 10 adds TensorialGaussianAvatar and GaussianAvatars as NeRSemble 2D-tracking comparators. The original depth and tracking comparator sets are retained; P3DMM in the new qualitative comparison was already evaluated in v1.

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce a neighborhood-loss control and a procedure deriving avatar-baseline tracks from optimized Gaussian deformations. Existing benchmark splits, metrics and training schedules are unchanged; newly specified COLMAP tuning details do not establish a revision to the original experiments.

E4.justification: v2 adds a neighborhood-consistency ablation, a COLMAP coverage-tuning analysis, and qualitative examinations of supervision, difficult generalization conditions and hair-motion/occlusion failures. These extend the retained ablations and microphone failure analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for the experiments. The added results follow the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1-8 retain their values. New Table 9 reports EPE 3.43 with neighborhood consistency versus 3.30 for Ours; Table 10 reports 7.21 for TensorialGaussianAvatar, 7.01 for GaussianAvatars and 5.20 for Ours. v2 also reports COLMAP coverage increasing from 77.5% to 80.3% under tuning and adds qualitative findings. These are additional results, not demonstrated changes to original benchmark performance.

T1.justification: Equations 1-6 retain the same mathematics; Equation 6 only reverses the order of additive terms. The added explanations and loss-ablation discussion introduce no formal definitions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The introduction and contribution list qualify the reconstruction claim as visible-surface reconstruction instead of broadly stating dense 4D reconstruction. The abstract, conclusion and principal method, dataset and performance contributions otherwise retain their meaning.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations attributing spatial coherence to DPT/shared transformer features and generalization to pretrained priors. It also specifically acknowledges unresolved individual-tooth and tongue tracking and unstable canonical predictions under extreme hair motion, supplementing the existing limitations.

D1.justification: Where v1 only states that COLMAP parameters were adjusted, v2 specifies a 20-subject validation split and tuning num_samples from 15 to 50 and window_radius from 5 to 9. It also clarifies that canonical coordinates use FLAME's canonical pose and neutral expression at metric scale. These are additional disclosures, not established changes to the underlying pipeline.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for Hallo3, CelebV-Text, GaussianAvatars and TensorialGaussianAvatar. Appendix D makes the distinction from DA3 and P3DMM more explicit, particularly arbitrary canonical 3D coordinates versus FLAME-bound UV coordinates, while retaining the existing related-work positioning.

P1.justification: Localized edits expand affiliations, introduce the Pixel3DMM abbreviation, explain loss roles and tighten dataset-construction prose. The appendix gains explanatory paragraphs, but the main narrative and section organization remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 9-10 and Figures 9, 10, 14 and 16. Existing figures are retained with appendix renumbering and reflow; the microphone failure figure now shares a page with new examples. The main visual organization remains stable.

improvement.justification: The added ablation and avatar comparisons strengthen empirical support, disclosed COLMAP settings improve reproducibility, and the visible-surface qualification and specific tracking limitations improve precision. These are useful, limited gains. The new generalization evidence remains qualitative, while the neighborhood loss is not precisely defined and the new tracking tables omit temporal margins.
